matchupOfTheWeek.title: Rush Offense vs. Run Defense
matchupOfTheWeek.description: Our rush offense grades 58/100 (about average) against CHI's run defense at 13/100 (among the NFL's worst) — the widest statistical edge on the board this week.

previewTake: Thursday night in Chicago presents a delicious mismatch on one side of the ball and a genuine test on the other. New England's about-average rushing attack (58/100) faces a Bears run defense that's borderline indefensible at 13/100—that's the widest edge we have all week, and we need to lean into it hard. The problem is Chicago's pass rush (94/100) is among the league's best, and we're heading into this game without Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown on the interior line—two significant losses that directly threaten Drake Maye's ability to operate. A.J. Brown's drop-plagued return and Romeo Doubs heading to IR mean our receiving corps are working through their own rough patch. Still, we're trending up (0.19 EPA/play over three games) against a Bears team sliding backward (-0.05), and we own a 4-1 record against them since 2010. This is winnable if our run game can punish that awful Chicago defense early and often.
